summary:
Session 2026-11-04.

Session 2026-11-04 (pre-open). Tuesday close: SPY +0.30%, QQQ +0.62%, XLK +1.31% (first up day after a -6.9% 5-day drop). Democrats swept both chambers in the midterms; futures rose after early losses. After-hours/premarket gaps: AMD +6-7% (Q4 guide ~$17B beat), ANET +12% (guide beat), SMCI +9%, AMGN -2 to -3% (biosimilar worries), BKNG down (revenue miss), SHOP -8.7% Tuesday, UBER -2% premarket (Q4 EPS guide 0.95-0.99 vs 1.06 Street; driver shortages, Middle East, AV spend; Q3 EPS slight miss). CVS announced a split into two companies by 2028; KHC to divest its NA coffee business. I did not chase the earnings gaps because they are priced in at the open. Opened a small 5% NOW long at about 112 as a stabilisation rebound: stop -9%, target +16%, horizon 12 days, p=0.52. The idea is a base at 106-112 after the -27% drop, and the AI-disruption fear in software looks overdone. Next session: check NOW's open and whether tech (FTNT 128, INTC 60.5, GOOGL 280, RDDT 96) keeps rebounding. If the market makes a second up close, consider adding to the rebound longs, but only with a catalyst. Also check whether Uber's weakness continues (drift short candidate) and CVS split reaction. Lesson so far: 4 cash sessions avoided losses in the knife-catching phase, but cash earns nothing, so small positions are fine once the tape stabilises.

prompt:
Your universe is every eligible US stock. Your style is a few high-quality trades.

- Look for situations where recent, specific information has not yet been reflected in the price:
  earnings surprises and guidance changes, contracts, regulatory decisions, management changes,
  supply problems, sector-wide shocks. Remember you trade at the open, after the overnight reaction,
  so ask what is still left to move, not what already moved. It works in both directions: bad
  news the price has not finished absorbing is a short.
- Prefer clear catalysts you can verify over vague narratives. A strong case beats a busy portfolio.
  A handful of positions at most is the expected shape; holding mostly cash is fine when your
  research turns up nothing compelling.
- Size positions by conviction and by how much could go wrong. Set stops and targets you would
  actually stand behind.
- Use the movers and most-active lists as places to start looking, not as reasons to buy.
